title: Whatever wrong we have done, Varuṇa, loosen it

words.context: Bhāskara: «मीञ् हिसायां … 'इदन्तो मसि'»; with pra, ‘to fail to keep’

sandhi.rule: t before c becomes c; t before h becomes d, and the h becomes dh

morphology.note: the Vedic 1st plural ending -masi for -maḥ; the second witness misreads it मिमीमसि (corrections.json).
the locative of दिव् ‘day’ (द्यवि), doubled to mean ‘every day’.

translation.literal: Whatever ordinance of yours, O god Varuṇa, we violate day after day, as people do —
translation.readable: Whatever law of yours, divine Varuṇa, we break day after day, as ordinary people will —

words.role: against whom the wrong is done
main verb of the first clause

words.meaning: we have effaced, we have obstructed
for the sin, on account of the fault

words.gram: reduplicated aorist injunctive, 2nd sg. active (with mā)

sandhi.rule: m before c becomes ñ; a + i becomes e
e + a becomes e, the a elided (written ऽ)
visarga before t becomes s; t before a vowel becomes d

morphology.note: the instrumental of अचित्ति with the Vedic ending -ī for -yā (Bhāskara: «'सुपां सुलुक्' इति पूर्वसवर्णः»).
the reduplicated aorist of √रिष् without augment, with the prohibitive मा.

translation.literal: Whatever offence this, O Varuṇa, we humans commit against the divine folk, whatever laws of yours we have effaced through thoughtlessness — do not harm us for that sin, O god.
translation.readable: Whatever wrong we humans do against the divine race, Varuṇa, whatever of your laws we have spoiled without knowing it — do not punish us, god, for that sin.

words.gram: f. loc. sg. (lengthened in the Saṃhitā)
indecl., emphatic particle (lengthened in the Saṃhitā)
words.context: Bhāskara: «'घ' इति पादपूरणः … 'ऋचि मनु' इत्यादिना संहितायां दीर्घत्वम्»
Bhāskara: «सत्यं बुद्धिपूर्वमेव कृतं पापम्», sin done deliberately
Bhāskara: «यत् न विद्म कृतमपि न जानीमः»

Bhāskara: «'निपातस्य च' इति संहितायां अथशब्दस्य दीर्घत्वम्»

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o; t before r becomes d; -uḥ before n becomes -ur

morphology.note: स्य, the imperative of √सो ‘to bind/loosen’, retroflexed after the preverb vi in the Saṃhitā; the word division keeps the recited form.
अथ lengthened in the Saṃhitā (P. 6.3.136 (निपातस्य च)); likewise घा for घ (P. 6.3.133 (ऋचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणाम्)).
the Vedic nominative plural in -āsaḥ (also in priyāsaḥ).

translation.literal: What gamblers have cheated, as in play, or what (we did) truly, and what we do not know — all those, O god, untie like loose (knots); then may we be dear to you, O Varuṇa.
translation.readable: Whatever wrong has been laid on us, as cheats do at dice, or done by us knowingly, or done without our knowing — loosen it all, god, like slack knots; and then, Varuṇa, may we be dear to you.

meaning: Three ṛks to Varuṇa that close the evening upasthāna. They are a confession: we break your laws day after day, as people will; we offend against the gods, knowingly or unknowingly; we are cheated by others, as in gambling. Varuṇa, who binds wrongdoers with his fetters, is asked not to punish but to loosen every knot, so that the worshipper may be dear to him again. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā they stand together at the end of 3.4.11 among the offering verses; in the Ṛgveda they are scattered: 1.25.1, 7.89.5 and 5.85.8. Bhāskara reads the gamblers as priests who serve their own ends («ऋत्विजः»), and the knowingly done sin as sin from lack of faith.
in_the_rite: Evening sūryopasthāna, after imaṃ me varuṇa and tat tvā yāmi, recited standing and facing west; the viniyoga is the one the Mylapore prayoga gives for the evening verses (vin-imam-me).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, on TS 3.4.11, reads the first verse as a promise of service rather than a confession: «यद्व्रतं यागादिकं कर्म वयं विशः मनुष्यमात्रभूताः द्यविद्यवि दिनेदिने प्रमिनीमसि प्रतर्कयामः अविच्छेदेनानुष्ठातुमिच्छामः» — though he also allows the plain sense, «यद्व्रतं प्रमिनीमः हिंसितवन्तः».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: On the second, the wrong is human carelessness, «मनुष्या वयं मनुष्यस्वभावात्संभाव्यमानप्रमादाः», and the prayer ends in grace: «मा रीरिषः, अपि तु अनुगृहाणैव».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: On the third: «कितवासः स्वार्थसाधनतत्पराः» — the cheats are those bent on their own gain; the sins are of three kinds, done by others to us, done deliberately («सत्यं बुद्धिपूर्वमेव कृतं पापमश्रद्धादिना»), and done without our knowing («कृतमपि न जानीमः»); untying them means forgiving them, «क्षमस्वेति यावत्».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: In the Saṃhitā kitavāsaḥ is an alternative offering verse: «तत्रैव याज्याविकल्पः - कितवास इति त्रिष्टुप्».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: The first verse is a gāyatrī, the second a jagatī (Bhāskara: «यत्किं चेदमिति जगती»), the third a triṣṭubh. The Ṛgveda has the same words (1.25.1; 7.89.5; 5.85.8, where it reads देवाधा for देवाथा).

notes.label: direct
notes.text: The base witness breaks यच्चिद्धि at a pañcāśat marker (यत् [45] चिद्धि); the edition joins it as sandhi requires (corrections.json).
